newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs off 5.04 pct on local selling - traders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs off 5.04 pct on local selling - traders.

text.p: Brazilian stocks were 5.04 percent lower in early trade on local selling, mostly driven by domestic mutual funds, traders said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active stocks were lower at 11,117 points at 1045 local time/1345 GMT. Total market turnover was 204.4 million reais ($189 million).
Brokers said local equity funds appear to be selling to cover future withdrawals from retail investors who are taking profits following the market recent strong volatility.
"It seems to be a preemptive measure to cover future withdrawals from individuals," said an equities desk manager.
Early this week, stock funds saw large outflows from individuals who were rattled by the market sharp weakness.
Such investors, they say, were mostly non-traditional participants in the stock market and were driven by the bolsa's stunning gains since the beginning of the year.

These investors were generally involved in fixed-income securities, but moved into stocks seeking higher returns as interest rates declined sharply after the introduction of the Real stabilization plan.
Foreign investors appear to be on the sidelines, traders said.
Benchmark Telebras preferred was down 5.1 percent at 139.50 reais.
In the spot commercial foreign exchange market, the real currency barely moved, slipping 0.03 percent to 1.0813 per dollar in calm trade, in contrast to the sharp stock slump.

Dollar inflows contributed to keeping the forex market calm, dealers said. On Thursday, financial and commercial foreign exchange contracts showed a $142.4 million surplus and dealers expect another surplus today.
In the futures markets, dollar and interest rates contracts were higher, partly due to the bolsa's sharp drop.
